new.title: See the Baltic and North Sea at the Ozeaneum
new.desc: The Ozeaneum on the Stralsund Hafeninsel belongs to the Deutsches Meeresmuseum foundation and shows Baltic and North Atlantic marine life in large aquariums. It sits beside the old brick harbour warehouses.
new.tip: Book timed tickets online and come early on weekends; allow two to three hours.

new.title: Admire the brick Gothic Marienkirche
new.desc: The Marienkirche on the Neuer Markt is one of the landmarks of north German brick Gothic and part of the UNESCO World Heritage old towns of Stralsund and Wismar. It was built in the 14th and 15th centuries.
new.tip: Free to enter; the church also has a concert programme with organ recitals.

new.title: Stand before the Rathaus on the Alter Markt
new.desc: The Stralsund town hall with its decorated north facade dates from the 13th century and was extended in the Hanseatic period. The cellar below, the Ratskeller, is widely described as one of the largest continuous cellars in northern Europe.
new.tip: The square is free to explore and lively in the evening.

new.title: Visit the Nikolaikirche beside the town hall
new.desc: St. Nikolai on the Alter Markt is the oldest of Stralsund's three big parish churches, built from the 13th century in the style of a Hanseatic merchant church. Inside are a rich Gothic interior and an astronomical clock.
new.tip: Entry is modest; combine it with the Rathaus visit.

new.title: Spot the Gothic gable of the Wulflamhaus
new.desc: The Wulflamhaus on the Alter Markt is a 14th-century brick merchant house with a richly stepped gable, named after the mayor Bertram Wulflam. It is one of the best-known secular Gothic buildings in the old town.
new.tip: Look at it from the square in the late afternoon light.

new.title: Go aboard the sail training ship Gorch Fock I
new.desc: Gorch Fock I was built in Hamburg in 1933 and sailed under the Soviet flag until 1999. Since 2003 she has been a museum ship in the Stralsund harbour, not to be confused with the current German Navy ship of the same name.
new.tip: The quay view is free; check opening times for boarding.
new.q: Gorch Fock I, Stadthafen, Hafenstraße, Stralsund

new.title: Explore the Marinemuseum on Dänholm island
new.desc: The Marinemuseum is on Dänholm, the island that became the cradle of the Prussian navy. It documents the naval history of the Baltic coast. The island is linked to the town by the Ziegelgrabenbrücke.
new.tip: Open in the summer season, roughly May to October, Tuesday to Sunday.

new.title: Drink a Störtebeker beer at the Braugasthaus
new.desc: The Braugasthaus belongs to the Störtebeker Braumanufaktur in the brewery quarter. It serves regional food with a beer matched to each dish by the staff.
new.tip: Try a hearty regional dish with the house beer; book ahead for weekends.

new.title: Join a Störtebeker brewery tour
new.desc: The Störtebeker Braumanufaktur brews beers under the German purity law and ties itself to the long brewing tradition of the Hanse city. Daily tours lead through the brewery quarter and end with a tasting.
new.tip: Tours are mostly in German; book in advance and check times.

new.title: Eat a Fischbrötchen at Fischkutter Anja
new.desc: Fish cutters moored at the Stralsund Stadthafen sell fresh fish rolls, smoked fish and fish and chips straight from the boat. Fischkutter Anja is among the busiest.
new.tip: Order a Backfisch or Matjes roll and expect a queue at lunchtime.

new.title: Dine in the Wulflamstuben on the Alter Markt
new.desc: Wulflamstuben is a restaurant on the ground floor of the 14th-century Wulflamhaus. It serves regional Pomeranian dishes in a historic setting on the main market square.
new.tip: Try the fish of the day.

new.title: Eat Baltic fish at Restaurant Lara
new.desc: Restaurant Lara is a brick building on the harbour opposite the Ozeaneum with a fish-centred menu and a view of the Hafeninsel.
new.tip: Good for lunch after the Ozeaneum; ask for the catch of the day.

new.title: Order Pomeranian fish at Zur Kogge
new.desc: Fischrestaurant Zur Kogge on Tribseer Straße is a fish restaurant listed for the Stralsund area.
new.tip: Try the fish platter with local herring or zander.

new.title: Stroll the Sundpromenade towards Parow
new.desc: The Sundpromenade follows the Strelasund shore from the Stralsund harbour to Parow, with views of the Rügen Bridge and the island of Dänholm.
new.tip: Flat and free; best at sunset.

new.title: Swim at the Schwämmi on Dänholm
new.desc: The island of Dänholm has a bathing beach called the Schwämmi on the Strelasund, reached over the Ziegelgrabenbrücke.
new.tip: Summer only.

new.title: Walk the Devin peninsula nature reserve
new.desc: The Devin peninsula in the Strelasund is a nature reserve with a hiking loop passing the ruins of a former brickworks.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes; the loop takes a couple of hours.

new.title: Sail the harbour on the Weiße Flotte
new.desc: The Weiße Flotte runs boat trips from the Stralsund harbour, including harbour tours and sailings towards Hiddensee and Rügen.
new.tip: Check the timetable at the quay; some sailings only run in summer.

new.title: Climb the tower of Dom St. Nikolai
new.desc: Greifswald's cathedral was built from the 13th century and is the baptismal church of Caspar David Friedrich. Its tower is the highest in the city and a popular lookout.
new.tip: Tower climb in season; the interior is free.

new.title: See Friedrich paintings in the Pommersches Landesmuseum
new.desc: The Pommersches Landesmuseum sits in the former Franciscan monastery and presents Pomeranian history from the Ice Age, with a Friedrich gallery. The Galerie der Romantik opened in December 2025.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; combine with the Friedrich-Zentrum ticket.

new.title: Visit Caspar David Friedrich's birthplace
new.desc: The Caspar-David-Friedrich-Zentrum on Lange Straße is in the painter's birthplace, a former soap boiler's house. It opened in 2004 and was extended in 2011.
new.tip: A combined ticket covers it and the Landesmuseum.

new.title: Wander through the Eldena abbey ruins
new.desc: The Cistercian abbey Eldena was founded in 1199; its ruin inspired Caspar David Friedrich. Entry is free and an open-air stage is built into it.
new.tip: Free access, nice at golden hour.

new.title: Watch the Wieck wooden drawbridge open
new.desc: The Wiecker Holzklappbrücke was built in 1887 in the Dutch style and is still hand-operated. It opens several times daily for sailing boats.
new.tip: Check opening times; stand on the quay at the harbour.

new.title: Photograph the Marktplatz and town hall
new.desc: Greifswald's Marktplatz with its Rathaus and gabled brick houses is the centre of the old town.
new.tip: Visit on market days (Wednesday and Saturday).

new.title: Eat smoked fish at Hafenräucherei WIE-05
new.desc: The Hafenräucherei WIE-05 is a harbour smokehouse restaurant of the fishing cooperative Greifswalder Bodden, serving fish rolls, smoked fish and soups.
new.tip: Try a smoked fish roll on the terrace by the harbour.

new.title: Dine harbourside at Zur Fähre in Wieck
new.desc: Restaurant Zur Fähre sits by the harbour near the railway bridge in Wieck and is recommended by guests.
new.tip: Order the fish of the day.

new.title: Try local fish at Gasthaus Fischer Hütter
new.desc: Gasthaus Fischer Hütter is a restaurant in the fishing village of Wieck, where restaurants serve freshly caught fish.
new.tip: Ask for the Bodden catch.
new.q: Gasthaus Fischer Hütter, An der Mühle 12, Greifswald-Wieck

new.title: Stroll the Museumshafen to the Fangenturm
new.desc: The Museumshafen has historic sailing vessels and the 13.5-metre Fangenturm, today the harbourmaster's office.
new.tip: Free; best on a sunny afternoon.

new.title: Walk through the thatched fishing village of Wieck
new.desc: Wieck keeps thatched fishermen's houses from the 18th and 19th centuries around its harbour.
new.tip: Combine with the bridge and a fish roll.
